title: Head injury or possible concussion
summary: Stop activity, monitor for danger signs, and prevent another head impact.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Concussion
CDC HEADS UP — Concussion Signs and Symptoms
actions: Keep the person still and stop sports, driving, or risky activity. Check breathing and control serious bleeding without pressing on a suspected skull fracture.

Call emergency services for loss of consciousness, increasing drowsiness, repeated vomiting, seizure, unequal pupils, weakness, slurred speech, severe worsening headache, blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears, or a high-energy injury.
If neck or spine injury is possible, support the head in the position found and avoid unnecessary movement.
A person with possible concussion should be assessed by a health professional and should not return to sport or hazardous work the same day.
Monitor for new or worsening symptoms. Normal sleep is generally allowed after medical advice when no danger signs are present; waking repeatedly is not routinely required.
prohibitions: Do not allow same-day return to sport after suspected concussion.
Do not leave a person with worsening symptoms alone.
Do not give alcohol, sedatives, or extra medication that could mask deterioration.

redFlags.text: Emergency warning signs selected—contact emergency services now.

emergencyCall.text: Call emergency services for worsening alertness, repeated vomiting, seizure, unequal pupils, drooping eyelid, face droop, limb weakness, slurred speech, severe worsening headache, or a dangerous mechanism.
